svg.title: Illustrative Service-Fee Yield by Property Rail
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-paid-case-yield-by-property-rail; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Illustrative Service-Fee Yield by Property Rail; subtitle: Compare dollars per completed paid case, not client asset balances.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Selected high-value cases only; these are constructed planning figures, not market averages. Assume 15 paid cases in each of five mutually exclusive property categories. A hypothetical permitted 10% fee connects the example balances to fee yields; actual fee bases, caps, timing, and agreements require state review.; caption: 15 × ($5,000 + $4,500 + $3,500 + $2,500 + $1,500) = $255,000 fees on $2,550,000 owner principal at the assumed rate.; stages: label: Corporate government warrants; value: $5,000 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 5000.0; detail: Illustrative $50,000 owner balance at 10%. Confirm that the warrant proceeds are actually state-held, then verify entity continuity and the officer's signing authority.; label: Business vendor checks; value: $4,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 4500.0; detail: Illustrative $45,000 owner balance at 10%. Reconcile supplier names, former addresses, and successor entities; exclude government warrants assigned to the preceding category.; label: Insurance proceeds; value: $3,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 3500.0; detail: Illustrative $35,000 owner balance at 10%. Resolve policyholder, beneficiary, and estate distinctions before requesting documents or representing a claimant's entitlement.; label: Securities-related cash; value: $2,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 2500.0; detail: Illustrative $25,000 recoverable cash balance at 10%. Confirm the state's recorded property form; do not price fees from a speculative current share-market valuation.; label: High-value wage balances; value: $1,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 1500.0; detail: Illustrative $15,000 owner balance at 10%. Screen for consolidated high-value balances; ordinary small payroll checks may not support manual recovery economics.

text.title: Illustrative Service-Fee Yield by Property Rail
text.tspan: Illustrative Service-Fee Yield by Property Rail

circle.title: label: Corporate government warrants; value: $5,000 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 5000.0; detail: Illustrative $50,000 owner balance at 10%. Confirm that the warrant proceeds are actually state-held, then verify entity continuity and the officer's signing authority.

label: Business vendor checks; value: $4,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 4500.0; detail: Illustrative $45,000 owner balance at 10%. Reconcile supplier names, former addresses, and successor entities; exclude government warrants assigned to the preceding category.

label: Insurance proceeds; value: $3,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 3500.0; detail: Illustrative $35,000 owner balance at 10%. Resolve policyholder, beneficiary, and estate distinctions before requesting documents or representing a claimant's entitlement.

label: Securities-related cash; value: $2,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 2500.0; detail: Illustrative $25,000 recoverable cash balance at 10%. Confirm the state's recorded property form; do not price fees from a speculative current share-market valuation.

label: High-value wage balances; value: $1,500 service fees per completed paid case; numeric value: 1500.0; detail: Illustrative $15,000 owner balance at 10%. Screen for consolidated high-value balances; ordinary small payroll checks may not support manual recovery economics.

text.title: Assumptions: Selected high-value cases only; these are constructed planning figures, not market averages. Assume 15 paid cases in each of five mutually exclusive property categories. A hypothetical permitted 10% fee connects the example balances to fee yields; actual fee bases, caps, timing, and agreements require state review.
